Definition: from G4149; wealthy; figuratively, abounding with:--rich.
BiblicalUsage: Plousios means rich, abounding with wealth. The rich man in Luke 16:19 was clothed in purple and fine linen and fared sumptuously every day, and Jesus says it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom, in Matthew 19:24 and Luke 18:25. James says, Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl, in James 5:1, and Laodicea said, I am rich, and knew not she was wretched, in Revelation 3:17.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe riches are a test, not a blessing in themselves — they can clothe a man in purple and leave him poor before God. That is why I hold that the only wealth that lasts is the kind laid up in heaven.
